stories.title: LA City Council Approves Largest-Ever Funding Pool for Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: The Los Angeles City Council voted unanimously to approve a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) backed by $466.6 million to build and renovate affordable housing. The largest pool of its kind in the city housing department’s history, pending approval by Mayor Karen Bass, the money will be distributed as grants and loans to developers, nonprofits and land trusts, the Los Angeles Times reported. With funding coming largely from Measure ULA, the so-called “mansion tax” enacted in 2022, the forthcoming NOFA represents the second round of the Homes for LA initiative. The first round, with grants awarded in April, provided nearly $361 million to support 5,241 affordable units across 80 projects, according to MyNewsLA.com. The NOFA is expected to be released Oct. 13, with applications closing on Dec. 4. The Los Angeles Housing Department will announce the recipients in February 2027, with the City Council reviewing and approving awards by April. bullets: LA City Council unanimously approves $466.6M affordable housing NOFA from Measure ULA tax revenue.
First round (April) funded 5,241 units across 80 projects with $361M; second round applications close Dec. 4.
Recipients announced Feb. 2027; LA Housing Dept. targeting dense affordable supply pipeline over 24+ months.
stories.summary: Los Angeles City Council approved a $466.6 million Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for affordable housing development, the largest in city history, funded primarily by Measure ULA mansion tax revenue enacted in 2022. The first round distributed $361 million to support 5,241 units across 80 projects in April. The second NOFA will open October 13 with applications closing December 4, with recipients announced in February 2027 and City Council approval by April.
stories.impact: Affordable housing supply flooding Los Angeles market will compress rent growth in sub-$1,800/month segments but may protect for-profit multifamily development by shifting subsidy-dependent units to nonprofits and CDCs, reducing political pressure on market-rate projects. Watch LA downtown and transit corridors (Metro) for aggressive affordable-first entitlement clustering that could raise mixed-income development costs and extend approvals timelines.

stories.title: Denver Arena Owner Planning Improvements, Mixed-Use Venture
stories.excerpt: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE) has committed to spending $135 million to renovate Ball Arena, the home arena for the Denver Nuggets and Colorado Avalanche. In addition, KSE has unveiled plans for a mixed-use project using some of the outdoor parking lots as building space. The Denver Business Journal reports the upgrades include a large glass façade, new escalators, a new team shop, a widening of arena concourses to decrease congestion, new point-of-sale technology and three new club spaces, including one that with access to 100-level seating. Plans also call for a 721-foot-long plaza and outdoor gathering area in the southeast area. KSE will use Perkins&Will as the project’s architect. It has also planned upgrades to its teams’ practice facilities, installing a 1,100-square-foot observation platform above the Nuggets’ practice court. KSE plans to redevelop dozens of acres of parking lots around Ball Arena. The company envisions turning the lots into a new neighborhood with office space, residential units, a performance venue and a hotel,. bullets: KSE commits $135M to Ball Arena renovation; 721-foot plaza and mixed-use parking lot redevelopment planned.

Major urban infill catalyst in Denver Lower Downtown near transit and sports anchor.
stories.summary: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE) announced a $135 million renovation of Ball Arena (Denver Nuggets/Avalanche home) including a new glass façade, expanded concourses, club spaces, and a major outdoor plaza. The project also calls for large-scale redevelopment of parking lots surrounding the arena into a new mixed-use neighborhood with office space, residential units, a performance venue, and hotel.
stories.impact: KSE's parking-lot-to-residential conversion unlocks significant multifamily opportunity in Denver's Lower Downtown, a high-demand submarket with sports/entertainment anchors and transit access. Development will lift land values and competition for sites; expect rapid entitlements and institutional capital chasing the Ball Arena catalyst. Secondary effect: hotel and office suites may compress short-term rental and flex-office demand, favoring traditional apartments.

stories.title: South Florida Starchitect Kobi Karp: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Kobi Karp, founder of Kobi Karp Architecture and Interior Design, has been designing buildings in South Florida for more than three decades. His portfolio includes projects such as Four Seasons at the Surf Club in Surfside, 1 Hotel South Beach, Four Seasons Fort Lauderdale, Wynwood 25 and Moxy Wynwood, and he has worked with many of the region’s most prominent developers over the course of his career. Commercial Observer recently caught up with the star architect to discuss his next big projects, the Live Local Act, and how development in South Florida has changed over the decades. And that is pretty phenomenal, because also the rents are traveling between $5 to $6 a foot. And the demand is substantial, and also what people are seeking in those buildings are amenities and functions that create a lifestyle. The people who rent there are in their early 20s to late 30s. A substantial amount are folks who have jobs in Downtown Miami and are looking to stay there for an extended period of time. So that’s a very interesting sort of scenario. The residents get up in the morning and they go to their offices and then come back in the afternoon. There are activities there for the people who live there, and they also bring their friends over. bullets: Kobi Karp, South Florida starchitect (30+ years), reports multifamily as primary active pipeline.
Miami River Flow project: 635 units, 80% leased in ~80 days at strong rent levels.
South Florida development renaissance anchored by luxury and mid-market residential conversion and new builds.
stories.summary: Kobi Karp, founder of a prominent South Florida architecture firm with a three-decade track record in residential and hospitality design, indicates that multifamily apartments are the primary financed and moving projects in his current pipeline. A recent 635-unit Miami River project operated by Flow achieved 80% occupancy in approximately 80 days with rents traveling above historical averages, signaling strong demand.
stories.impact: South Florida multifamily market is heating up with rapid absorption and rent momentum, particularly along Miami River and prime submarkets where starchitects cluster high-design, branded apartments. Mana/Griffin Wynwood acquisition rumors and Mana's diversification into Fort Lauderdale suggest institutional capital sees South Florida as undervalued relative to supply-constrained coastal demand; expect competitive bidding and rising land prices for prime multifamily sites.

stories.title: BHI Lends $72M on New Jersey Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Prestige Development and Anak Development has landed $71.5 million of construction financing to build a multifamily project in northern New Jersey, Commercial Observer has learned. BHI, the U.S Branch of Bank Hapoalim, provided the loan for the sponsorship’s 250-unit The Standard apartment community in Bayonne, N.J. Maven Capital’s Sean Shahkohi negotiated the financing. David Kesselman, vice president of commercial real estate at BHI, said in a statement that the Bayonne project will “expand the local housing supply and meet growing demand.” Located at 197 Avenue East steps from 22nd Street Station on the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail line, the apartment property will feature a mix of studio to two-bedroom units, a 227-space parking garage and roughly 1,950 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Community amenities will include a swimming pool, sundeck, fitness center, yoga room, sauna, coworking areas, golf simulator and dog walk. Michael Shahkohi, principal of Prestige Development, said in a statement that BHI understood when executing the loan “both the complexity of construction execution and the long-term vision” of the project. The Standard project was designed by MHS Architecture and is situated at the former site of the Villanova Catering Hall. It is slated for completion in summer 2027. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BHI (Bank Hapoalim U.S. Branch) closes $71.5M construction loan for The Standard, Bayonne, N.J.
Prestige Development and Anak Development: 250-unit mixed studio-to-2BR on Hudson-Bergen Light Rail at 22nd St.
Transit-oriented infill in Hudson County with retail, parking, and high-end amenities near NYC commute corridor.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Prestige Development and Anak Development secured $71.5 million in construction financing from BHI for The Standard, a 250-unit multifamily community in Bayonne, New Jersey. The project is located at 197 Avenue East steps from the 22nd Street Station on the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail, featuring studio to two-bedroom units, 227-space parking garage, ground-floor retail, and resort-style amenities.
stories.impact: Hudson County NJ continues attracting construction financing as transit-proximate alternative to Manhattan and Brooklyn for price-sensitive renters. Light Rail access and proximity to 22nd St. Station will drive commuter demand; watch for rental pricing pegged to PATH/NJ Transit commute-sheds rather than local job centers. Positive signal for regional lender appetite for transit-oriented New Jersey multifamily; capacity exists despite higher rates.

stories.title: Data Center Developer Pays $14.7M for S. Phoenix Parcel
stories.excerpt: GI Partners recently paid $14.7 million for land just south of Phoenix that it plans to develop a data center on. LKY was the seller of the 5.4-acre parcel. The Phoenix Business Journal report LKY paid $3.15 million for the land in 2012. The site is located right next to an APS substation, and LKY says it has worked with APS for years to expand that substation to support a future data center. Phoenix concluded a data center project would be allowed on the site. LKY Development Company, Inc. specializes in acquiring and entitling subdivisions and master plan communities. GI Partners is a private alternatives investment firm with a handful of offices, including Scottsdale. The firm has raised more than $49 billion in capital from leading institutional investors worldwide to invest in private equity, real estate, and data infrastructure strategies. stories.summary: GI Partners, a major private alternatives investment firm, acquired a 5.4-acre parcel just south of Phoenix for $14.7 million to develop a data center. The seller, LKY Development, had purchased the land in 2012 for $3.15 million and worked with APS (Arizona Public Service) to expand the adjacent substation to support future data center operations. Phoenix has already approved the data center use.
stories.impact: Data center capital redeployment away from multifamily signals market saturation and venture capital rotation toward infrastructure. Phoenix submarket will see utility corridor and industrial-zoned land appreciate, potentially crowding out multifamily site assembly. No direct demand impact on apartments, but indirectly compresses land availability for mixed-use or urban infill development and may push multifamily investment southwestward toward less competitive submarkets.

stories.title: Coworking Firm Industrious to Provide Hologram-Like Google Beam Meetings
stories.excerpt: Industrious, a major flexible workplace company, announced Thursday that it has partnered with Google to launch a network of Google Beam meeting rooms exclusively for its members and guests. Google’s HP Dimension with Google Beam bills itself as an artificial intelligence-first video communication platform that renders meeting participants in their true size, positioned as if they were sitting around the same table. Spatial audio anchors each voice directly to the speaker, so people look, sound and feel more like they’re in the same room without headsets or complex setup, according to the announcement. The rooms will be available in New York City, Chicago, Atlanta and Palo Alto, Calif., starting in October. Industrious locations with Google Beam will include those at Tower 49 in New York City, Ponce City Market in Atlanta, the Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago and East Palo Alto. “What makes Beam special is how natural the conversation feels,” Carlos Becil, chief product officer at Industrious, said in an email to Commercial Observer. “The person across from you appears at their true size, their voice comes from where they’re sitting, and you can read the facial expressions and subtle cues that help people connect naturally. “We’re excited about this partnership because it means we can offer our members a face-to-face experience across cities thousands of miles apart,” Becil added. “That is something quite new, and we’re excited to see how our members use it. The rooms with Google Beam are complimentary for Industrious members and bookable for nonmembers. The pricing will be similar to our other bookable conferencing-enabled spaces.” Any Industrious guest can book an HP Dimension with Google Beam session on demand, while Industrious members receive priority scheduling alongside their everyday workspaces and collaboration tools. No measurable impact on apartment development underwriting or market dynamics.

stories.title: Wealth Management Firm Cerity Expands at 99 Park Ave.
stories.excerpt: Cerity Partners LLC, a national wealth management and financial advisory firm, has expanded its headquarters at Global Holdings’ 99 Park Ave., bringing its total footprint at the Midtown office tower to 68,271 square feet. The expansion follows the completion of Global Holdings’ $30-million capital improvement program earlier this year and brings the 600,000-square-foot tower to 98% leased. The tenant signed a 15-year lease for 19,600 square feet on a portion of the eighth floor, adding to its existing 48,671-square-foot footprint across the 15th and 16th floors. The deal marks Cerity’s second expansion at the property in less than a year. “Cerity Partners’ continued growth at 99 Park Ave. reflects the strength of our investment in the building and the workplace we’ve created,” said Alexander Radmin, director of leasing at Global Holdings Management Group. Cerity was represented by Nicholas Dysenchuk and Rob Lowe of Cushman & Wakefield. Global Holdings was represented by Radmin, along with Paul Glickman, Diana Biasotti, Kristen Morgan and Harrison Potter of JLL. stories.summary: Cerity Partners LLC, a national wealth management and financial advisory firm, expanded its headquarters at Global Holdings' 99 Park Ave. (Midtown Manhattan) with a new 19,600-square-foot lease on the eighth floor for 15 years, bringing its total footprint to 68,271 square feet. The expansion follows Global Holdings' $30 million capital improvement program and brings the 600,000-square-foot tower to 98% occupancy.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. Office leasing strength in prime Midtown reflects wealth management sector resilience but does not alter residential demand drivers or relocation patterns. Secondary effect: sustained office capital expenditure in trophy buildings may signal institutional confidence in NYC office recovery, potentially supporting residential rents through corporate hiring and talent retention.

stories.title: AI Software Company Signs Cambridge’s Largest Office Lease of 2026
stories.excerpt: Blitzy, the autonomous software development company founded in Cambridge in 2023, has signed a 52,000-square-foot office lease at One Kendall Square, expanding and keeping its headquarters in its origin city. The transaction is the largest new office lease completed in Cambridge in 2026, according to JLL, which represented Blitzy. The lease covers two floors at Building 200 at One Kendall Square and runs five years, with Blitzy expected to take occupancy in the second quarter of of 2027 following a 39,000-square-foot build-out. The building is owned by ARE-MA REGION NO. 59, LLC, an affiliate of Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc. “It’s no mystery that the Cambridge office market has been particularly hard hit during the last 6 years, but the green shoots are there, with AI companies like Blitzy driving that early momentum and representing over 60% of the new leasing volume across the city year to date,” said Bryan Sparkes, senior managing director at JLL. stories.impact: Cambridge office recovery driven by AI tenant concentration signals potential residential demand lift in Kendall Square and nearby neighborhoods (Somerville, Watertown) as high-paid AI engineering talent clusters. Watch for premium multifamily rents ($2,200+/2BR) near transit and walkable-to-Kendall neighborhoods; May also compress existing office conversions to residential as institutional investors pivot toward new AI office demand, reducing conversion supply and multifamily delivery.

stories.title: Moishe Mana Buys Discounted Fort Lauderdale Office Tower for $89M
stories.excerpt: Moishe Mana has ventured out of Miami and into Fort Lauderdale, nabbing a discount to buy a 30-story office building for $89 million, property records show. Called 110 Tower, the 777,248-square-foot property was built in 1987 adjacent to Broward County’s court building at 110 Southeast Sixth Street in the city’s downtown. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $66.3 million acquisition loan. The purchase marks a shift for Mana, who is the largest landowner in Downtown Miami and the city’s Wynwood neighborhood, where he is known for buying properties every few months. Just this year, the mogul purchased an office tower in Downtown Miami for $110 million and the retail building housing the popular Pastis French bistro in Wynwood for nearly $25 million. Mana is rumored to be selling much of his Wynwood portfolio to Citadel billionaire Ken Griffin in a blockbuster deal worth as much as $1 billion. Some suspect the recent acquisition spree is part of a 1031 exchange ahead of the pending Wynwood transaction, though both Mana and Griffin have denied that a deal is in the works. The former owner of Fort Lauderdale’s 110 Tower, Chicago-based GEM Realty Capital, purchased the 1.72-acre asset for $112.9 million in 2016, representing a 21 percent decline in value from the recent sale price. The Broward County office market has been slower to recover from the pandemic than Miami-Dade and Palm Beach counties, which have attracted well-heeled, new-to-market tech and finance companies. Mana and representatives for GEM Realty Capital did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Moishe Mana acquires 110 Tower, Fort Lauderdale: $89M for 777k SF office (30-story, built 1987).
City National Bank of Florida provided $66.3M acquisition loan; downtown location near Broward courts.
Mana diversifying beyond Miami (largest Downtown/Wynwood landholder) amid $1B rumored Wynwood sale to Ken Griffin.
stories.summary: Real estate mogul Moishe Mana purchased 110 Tower, a 777,248-square-foot, 30-story office building in Fort Lauderdale's downtown for $89 million. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $66.3 million acquisition loan. The purchase marks a geographic diversification for Mana, who is the largest landholder in Downtown Miami and Wynwood.
stories.impact: Mana's Fort Lauderdale entry signals distressed or undervalued office asset accumulation, likely part of 1031 exchange activity ahead of rumored Wynwood portfolio sale to Ken Griffin. Watch for follow-on Fort Lauderdale office-to-multifamily conversions by Mana or Griffin (Citadel HQ Miami Beach); expect aggressive adaptive-reuse and renovation strategies that will tighten downtown FLL residential supply and elevate construction cost benchmarks in the submarket. Downtown FLL multifamily will see capital competition and land value appreciation.

stories.title: Starbucks to Close 250 North American Stores Amid Massive Overhaul
stories.excerpt: The “Back to Starbucks” overhaul isn’t over yet. Seattle-based coffee giant Starbucks announced Thursday that it will close 250 stores across North America this week in its second round of mass closures since Brian Niccol took over as chairman and CEO in 2024. Mike Grams, Starbucks’ chief operating officer, said in a letter to employees that locations on the chopping block are underperforming financially or unable to deliver Starbucks’ desired experience for customers and employees, the Associated Press reported. The announcement did not specify which among North America’s roughly 18,300 Starbucks locations are due to close. The last wave of closures came a little more than a year ago, when Starbucks cut 627 North American and European stores alongside 900 non-retail employees. This May, the company announced another 300 layoffs affecting its U.S. corporate employees and the closure of underused regional offices. The bold steps to rehabilitate the struggling brand were part of Niccol’s $1 billion restructuring plan, dubbed “Back to Starbucks.” The move came amid declining sales, increased competition and a rising tide of unionization by its retail employees. The workers union Starbucks Workers United formed in late 2021 and has spread to 700 U.S. stores. No labor agreement has been yet reached between the union and Starbucks. Aside from store closures, the company-wide revamp has included thousands of store retrofits — 1,500 of which are due to be completed by Sept. 30, according to Grams. His letter on Thursday said that the company remains committed to growing its North American store count as well. The progress gave the company “a clearer view” of how its coffeehouses were performing. “While most are benefiting from this overall momentum, some coffeehouses continue to underperform despite the hard work and commitment of all of you,” Grams wrote in his letter. bullets: Starbucks announces closure of 250 North American stores in second wave under CEO Brian Niccol's 'Back to Starbucks.'
Locations underperforming or unable to deliver brand experience; prior wave (2024) closed 627 stores, plus 300 corporate layoffs.
Total restructuring commitment: $1B overhaul; ~18,300 North American Starbucks remain after closures.
stories.summary: Starbucks announced the closure of 250 North American stores this week as part of CEO Brian Niccol's $1 billion "Back to Starbucks" restructuring plan. The closures target underperforming locations and those unable to deliver the Starbucks customer and employee experience. This marks the second major wave of closures since Niccol's appointment in 2024; a prior closure round in 2024 eliminated 627 stores and 900 non-retail employees.
stories.impact: Retail footprint contraction reduces ground-floor retail demand in multifamily mixed-use projects nationwide. Developers underpinning residential economics with coffee-shop anchor tenants face heightened risk of co-tenancy defaults and rent reductions. Watch for secondary retail voids in street-level multifamily mixed-use across secondary markets; may depress overall property valuations and cap rates for new constructions with retail dependency. Strong multifamily submarkets with alternative retail anchors (grocers, fast-casual, health) will weather the shift; weak-density submarkets face retail vacancy headwinds.
